title: add runtime NVTX ranges, counters, microbench instrumentation and perf dashboard
author: Evan Park
description:
Motivation: Improve runtime visibility for kernel selection, scheduling, KV cache hot-paths and continuous batching by adding NVTX ranges and lightweight counters, plus a microbench harness and a Grafana dashboard. This enables fast correlation of latency regressions to scheduling and kernel decisions and provides a repeatable microbench for kernel-level comparisons.

What this PR does: adds NVTX ranges around hot runtime stages (request dispatch, batching, kernel launch, KV cache hit/miss, kv cache eviction), introduces per-worker counters (bytes_batched, requests_queued, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, kernel_launch_count), implements a small microbench harness under tools/microbench that can run sequence-length and batch-size sweeps on CI and locally, and publishes a Grafana dashboard (observability/perf_dashboards/runtime_nvtx.json) plus documentation in docs/perf/telemetry.md.

Implementation notes: NVTX integration is gated behind a build-time flag (ENABLE_NVTX) and runtime env REDWOOD_NVTX_ENABLED, default off in CI to avoid noise. Counters are provided via the existing metrics registry (metering-compatible) with new labels for model, device, and schedule_type. Microbench uses a reproducible RNG seed and mock model backend that exercises kernels with representative token distributions. Dashboard uses aggregated job labels and example panels for NVTX timing breakdown, counter rates over time, and microbench run comparisons.

Backward compatibility: No API surface changes. Telemetry flag off by default. Dashboard and docs are additive.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for counter increments and NVTX range lifetimes, end-to-end microbench CI job (only on perf-canary) that runs a small sweep and uploads results to the perf artifact bucket. Local benchmark numbers included in the PR comment show ~8-12% variance reduction in tail latency after KV cache hot-path tracing allowed tuning of the scheduler batching window.

Files changed (high level): src/runtime/scheduler.cpp, src/runtime/kv_cache.cpp, src/runtime/kernel_launcher.cpp, src/runtime/telemetry/nvtx_wrapper.h, src/runtime/telemetry/counters.h, tools/microbench/runner.cc, tools/microbench/configs/*.yaml, observability/perf_dashboards/runtime_nvtx.json, docs/perf/telemetry.md, ci/perf-canary/workflows/microbench.yml, examples/telemetry/trace_reader.py

How to review: focus on correctness of NVTX scope boundaries, ensuring counters increment on all fast paths, and microbench reproducibility. The dashboard JSON is large but low-risk (visual only) — reviewers can load it into Grafana via the README instructions.

Related: copies/extends patterns from previous PRs that added NVTX in specific components (see PRs 41258, 42311).

review_comments: Aisha Kapoor: please ensure NVTX scopes are minimal and do not wrap allocations — NVTX can skew allocation tracing. Also annotate which kernels are async vs sync.
Evan Park: addressed, reduced scope of NVTX around allocations and added explicit 'async' tag where kernel launcher schedules work (see scheduler.cpp diff).
Miguel Torres: counters look good; prefer exponential backoff when kv_cache misses spike to avoid thundering herd. Can we add a simple backoff counter?
Evan Park: added a lightweight miss_spike_backoff counter and a scheduling guard; microbench shows it stabilizes batch sizes under pathological inputs.
Lena Fischer: unit tests look good. Please add a small CLI flag to microbench to skip network upload for local runs.
Evan Park: added --no-upload to microbench runner and documented it in README.telemetry.md.
CI: perf-canary job initially failed (timeout in microbench run), re-ran with increased timeout and it passed.
Codeowner approval: Aisha Kapoor approved, Miguel Torres approved.
performance_summary: Local microbench (seq_len=512, batch=8) before: p99=42.3ms, after: p99=38.1ms (~9.9% improvement)
Continuous batching experiments show reduced variance in p95/p99 when scheduler batching window tuned after NVTX analysis
KV cache instrumentation revealed a ~3% additional overhead in miss paths (expected) but enabled a policy change that recovered 5% net improvement in throughput for mixed workloads
release_notes: Added runtime NVTX ranges and counters for improved profiling, a microbench harness for kernel/scheduler comparisons, and a Grafana dashboard for visualizing runtime NVTX timing and counters. Instrumentation is behind a flag and off by default.
merge_summary: Squash merged after approvals. CI green. Microbench artifacts uploaded to perf bucket. Dashboard added to repo for cluster owners to import.
notes_for_ops: ENABLE_NVTX is build-time; to enable at runtime set REDWOOD_NVTX_ENABLED=1 and ensure workers have nvtx library available
Perf-canary pipeline has a new microbench job that runs on the perf matrix; see ci/perf-canary/workflows/microbench.yml
Grafana dashboard ID: runtime_nvtx_v1 — cluster owners can import observability/perf_dashboards/runtime_nvtx.json
